fieldValues.title: 7. Review and land: what we tried and where we went too far
fieldValues.thinking_reached:
The ideal: Each change arrives as a pull request someone can judge, is checked and reviewed by someone else, and lands safely; closed means landed.

What we have tried: Gates by exit code; the srs Mode, Cell and Door check; gate:auto-merge and gate:owner-merge; merge rights by mode and door (decision 949ae72d); quorum review by another member; five PR templates; clerk ground and the steward's false-close guard; muDemocracy.org's provenance check.

Problems recorded here: SP-71, SP-110, SP-112, SP-60, SP-63.
fieldValues.tensions:
- Line 1, Review each change and merge on green: too far toward Review each change. Every one of 254 merges in the week to 2026-10-23 went through the owner (audit); srs#962 merged while its challenger verdict was reject.
- Line 2, Repository checks and one definition of a good PR: too far toward Repository checks. 11 of the last 20 merged srs PR bodies would fail the classification check (finding 157dc2a3); a four-line doc PR was blocked on 2026-10-25 (srs#975).
- Line 3, A reviewer's judgement and encoded gates: too far toward both a reviewer's judgement and encoded gates, by turns. A PR can carry an authority decision unnoticed (SP-71); a closed issue does not mean the work landed (SP-60).
fieldValues.unresolved_questions:
- The three tensions are a first pass: none has its four 2×2 cases or the cube filled yet (handbook, A domain's axes, steps 3 and 4).
- Is each tension orthogonal to the other two in this stage, and which pole is yang here: does it flip from the parent domain?
fieldValues.next_action: Fill the 2×2 cases from the stage's own history; then name the remedy that moves us back out of each shadow.
